A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RadZero research, with matching authors, architecture, datasets and retained results. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout all 15 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2, including their appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original RadZero classification, grounding and segmentation results in Tables 1–4, alongside component ablations and qualitative analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional component and alignment-method experiments in Table 5.

M1.justification: The encoders, two added Transformer layers, finding-sentence extraction, contrastive losses and inference pipeline are retained; VL-CABS names the existing similarity-based attention. However, v1 Figure 3 pools L2-normalized vision tokens, whereas v2 Section 3.2.2 pools unnormalized v_ik. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is an intended procedural change or an omitted normalization bar.

E1.justification: Training remains on MIMIC-CXR. Evaluation retains Open-I, PadChest/PadChest20, ChestXray14, CheXpert, ChestXDet10, SIIM, RSNA and MS-CXR for the same classification, grounding and segmentation tasks. Added analyses use existing coverage; lower-resolution model configurations do not introduce a new task or population.

E2.justification: v2 adds G2D to the segmentation comparison in Table 4, using attributed results. New Table 5 evaluates LiT and dino.txt alongside CARZero under common settings; v1 discussed LiT and dino.txt without reporting such evaluations. This substantially expands direct comparisons with alternative alignment approaches while retaining the original benchmark baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds 224-pixel configurations to the main comparisons and introduces Table 5's controlled sequence varying similarity function, trainable layers, multi-positive supervision and resolution. It also reports alignment-method comparisons with other settings held identical. Existing dataset splits, metrics, threshold searches and documented training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5.4 and Table 5 directly test dot-product versus cosine similarity and combine component controls with alternative alignment methods across classification and spatial tasks. Appendix A adds a CARZero attention-map case study. v1's standalone multi-positive comparison is removed, with a different comparison reported at 224 pixels; the view-position, encoder, layer-depth, text-encoder and batch-size appendix studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional results follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing main benchmark rows remain numerically unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results for controlled alignment comparisons and the 224-pixel model, including 0.537 ChestXDet10 grounding accuracy and 0.562 RSNA Dice. Table 4 adds G2D Dice scores of 0.477 on RSNA and 0.051 on SIIM. v1 Table 6's random-selection results disappear. These are added or removed experimental results, not same-setting improvements to the retained RadZero scores.

T1.justification: Most equations in v2 restate v1's pseudocode, and the contrastive losses remain equivalent. However, the attended-embedding definition in Section 3.2.2 uses raw tokens rather than the normalized tokens pooled in v1 Figure 3. As written, this is a limited, non-equivalent mathematical change whose intent is unresolved. Neither version contains theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim explainable similarity-based alignment, strong zero-shot classification, grounding and segmentation, and qualitative open-vocabulary segmentation capability. Naming the attention mechanism VL-CABS emphasizes an existing contribution without establishing a new core capability or changing the principal claims.

C2.justification: v2 uses the lower-resolution results to argue that gains extend beyond resolution and suggests that matching encoder pretraining resolution explains classification performance. Appendix A expands the interpretation of attention maps and their dependence on ground-truth context. The conclusion newly acknowledges dependence on the pretrained encoder. The explicit ribs-as-spine failure discussion is removed, while boundary imprecision and the calcification limitation remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 newly states that the extraction LLM runs in a private computing environment. The two-Transformer-layer configuration stated there was already disclosed in v1 Appendix C. Training hyperparameters, hardware, training time, extraction prompt and data-processing access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds G2D and discusses its attention-derived pseudo-mask supervision. It also adds Wang et al.'s Learning Low-Rank Feature for Thorax Disease Classification to the introduction. The existing relationships to LiT, dino.txt, UniCLIP and medical alignment methods remain broadly intact despite substantial rewriting.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method description and results discussion are extensively rewritten. v2 introduces VL-CABS terminology and dataset abbreviations, replaces pseudocode with equations, folds the separate explainability discussions into other sections, adds main-text Section 5.4 and reorganizes the appendices.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from two-column to predominantly single-column layout, adds the introductory attention-versus-similarity illustration and Appendix A visualization, merges framework and inference diagrams, and combines segmentation panels. Benchmark tables gain rows, Table 5 is added, the pseudocode figure is removed, and retained appendix tables and visualizations are extensively rearranged.

improvement.justification: The added 224-pixel comparisons and Table 5 better isolate the contributions of similarity, supervision, architecture and resolution, strengthening evidence for the retained claims. Appendix A also makes the interpretability argument more concrete. These gains outweigh the loss of the earlier standalone multi-positive comparison, but the new pooling-normalization discrepancy weakens mathematical clarity and reproducibility, limiting the overall improvement.
